title: MIsCORE-RIUD: Survival Without Representational Identity in Black-Hole Merger Dynamics
content: RIUD Papers V–VII tested different consequences of an already-frozen merger-local population system: survival outside the residual frontend, reduction to simpler predictive or source-side variables, and interchangeability of detector representations. The present manuscript performs a frozen secondary analysis of those results and asks a new question: are representation survival, representational identity, and predictive/mechanistic reduction empirically equivalent properties? They are evaluated as separate logical propositions without pooling their statistics or rebuilding the lower-order object.Paper V provides scoped survival outside the residual frontend: in the availability-defined RAW17 branch, ONPATH>OFFPATH holds in 15/17 raw H1/L1 pairs, NULL200 rarity in 16/17, and both criteria in 15/17. Its strongest tested known-physics surrogate recovers 82.6449% of the frozen likelihood improvement, but nested cross-validation does not yield a stable replacement.Paper VI then attacks reduction directly. In 91-event pre-transition out-of-fold prediction, direction accuracy is 0.3956 and net-rate Spearman rho=0.0416, with null p=0.683 and 0.264; geometry adds no incremental support. A verified direct-GR representation gives DeltaLL=+0.2243 against +5.3370 for the frozen reference, while source-native SXS PATH continuity survives center steps of 5, 10, and 15 ms in 10/10 cases and 20 ms in 9/10.Paper VII attacks identity. Event-blocked detector prediction gives median gain -0.2044 for H1-to-L1 and +0.6497 for L1-to-H1; the latter has 0/9,999 whole-event null exceedances, corresponding to a plus-one p=0.0001. Relative high-band balance reverses from median log10(L1/H1)=+0.4373 at 10 ms to -0.7916 at 80 ms, while higher-order PATH persists across a substantial lower-order support sweep.The combined frozen evidence therefore supports survival without representational identity and survival without stable reduction under the tested contracts. This is a relational invariance claim, not a universal waveform identity, a universal K-sector equation, a native SXS replay of R40, or a claim that lower-order representation is irrelevant.
